title: Redefine table resize rail and sorting/filter mental models for lazy-rendered grids
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Our virtualized table handles very wide datasets but users report surprising behavior when resizing columns, reordering, or applying sorts/filters while the table is lazily rendering rows. Resize handles feel disconnected when the visible viewport is a subset of the model-backed columns; sorting and filter states are not visually discoverable during heavy virtualization churn.

Goal: Create a cohesive UX mental model for interaction with large virtualized grids that: (1) makes column resize feel anchored and predictable even for off-screen rows, (2) surfaces active sort/filter state robustly during incremental rendering, (3) provides density presets mapped to token scale and preserves user preferences across sessions, and (4) maintains keyboard-first accessibility and minimal layout jank.

Constraints: Must be implementable with current React table primitives and the runtime's incremental virtualization patterns. Avoid solutions that require client-side complete materialization of very wide tables. Keep perf overhead under ~6% p50 render cost for typical 1k-row workloads. Conform to Redwood tokens for spacing, focus rings, and motion durations.

Deliverables: design specs (Figma), a small interaction prototype (storybook), acceptance criteria and QA script, and an accessibility review checklist.
acceptance_criteria: Resize rail visual affordance stays aligned to logical column header even when cells are virtualized off-screen
Resizing uses snapping thresholds consistent with density tokens and persists per-user for the session
Sort and filter chips remain visible in the header area and have a compact collapsed state during heavy virtualization to avoid layout thrash
Keyboard handling: header focus + arrow + modifier keys allow resizing and reordering without pointer support
Prototype in Storybook that simulates 50ms row hydration latency and demonstrates no >6% median render cost increase
Design handoff with tokens: spacing, hover/active colors, motion timings and aria annotations
steps: Audit current table variants for all usages in Console and Quickstart templates
Run perf microbenchmarks with 500/1k/5k row synthetic loads to measure baseline
Create low-fidelity interaction flows showing resize rail behavior during incremental row hydration
Iterate on Figma designs with engineering for feasible DOM structure and transform layers
Build Storybook prototype that toggles virtualization lag, density presets and keyboard-first flows
Run accessibility review and update focus/announce patterns
Handoff: token map, CSS snippets, and engineering acceptance tests
engineering_notes: Prefer transform-based virtualization (translateY) to avoid layout passes when shifting rows
Keep a lightweight header sync layer: header state should be decoupled from the row render tree so resize calculations use model positions, not DOM positions
Debounce resize calculations by 80ms on pointermove; apply final layout immediately on pointerup
Expose a stabilization mode in the table runtime for canary testing where rendering waits for header state to settle for 50ms
Quantitative goal: p50 tokenization + layout overhead <= 6% for 1k rows on c5.large type dev machines
PR template: include a perf screenshot (devtools FPS + virtualized frame times) and a11y lint results
decision_log: 2026-03-11: Choose model-positioned resize anchor rather than DOM-pixel anchor to avoid mismatch during lazy hydration
2026-03-12: Use compact header chips (replace sort icon + text with single token chip) when virtualization load exceeds threshold of 24ms/frame
2026-03-13: Persist density choice in localStorage keyed by project to avoid cross-project leakage; server-side persistence deferred to a later epic
2026-03-14: Keyboard-first interactions confirmed as default; pointer gestures are additive and must mirror key behavior
comments: 2026-03-11 - Liam O'Connor: Spiked a prototype using header model anchors. Early results show a visible 10px jump when virtualization offsets change; follow-up: compute virtual column offsets from model metadata instead of reading DOM rectangles.
2026-03-12 - Maya Patel (PM): Reviewed prototypes with Growth team. They asked for a mode that auto-collapses wide filter panels when the table width is under 800px — added to 'nice-to-have'.

2026-03-12 - Ana Rodriguez (Engineering): Noted that current table runtime doesn't expose column width history per session. Suggest adding a small LRU cache keyed by table-id + user to persist adjustments.
2026-03-13 - Accessibility review (Ravi Shah): Header chips need aria-live region updates when sort or filter changes during virtualization to inform screen reader users of transient state changes.
2026-03-14 - Design critique: Reduced motion variant introduced; need to ensure snapping thresholds still feel natural when motion is disabled. Liam to prototype with reduced motion tokens.
